newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa board says to end maize mkt intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa board says to end maize mkt intervention.

text.p: South Africa's state-owned Maize Board said on Thursday all statutory intervention in the maize market would end on April 30, 1997, the last day of the current season.
The announcement follows a meeting on Thursday of the Maize Advisory Committee, a grouping representing maize industry interests, where agreement was reached on this move.

The official announcement from the board, which controlled the maize market for almost 70 years, follows Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom's decision in November last year to abolish a floor price and price stabilisation from the start of the 1997/98 season on May 1.

"All statutory intervention will be terminated on April 30, that is, there will be no levies and no marketing intervention," said Leon du Plessis, the general manager of the Maize Board and acting chairperson of the committee.
This move signals the demise of the Maize Board, but du Plessis told Reuters the body may continue to exist beyond April 30 due to the logistics of winding down its functions.
"The liquidation of the board may still take one or two months (after that)," he said.

The committee said in a statement it was unanimously agreed that upon termination of the board its net assets would be placed in a special trust. Monies would be used to fund activities accepted by the minister.
These activities would be recommended by the National Agricultural Marketing Council, a body appointed in terms of the new Marketing of Agricultural Marketing Products Act.

The committee said it had appointed a working group to look into the best possible ways to provide industry services, including market information, grading regulations, sanitary and phyto-sanitary measures and registration of cultivars.
These services were previously carried out by the Maize Board.
